member_targets: The typical acceleration distance (a quantity of run-up length) an outgoing relay runner requires to reach the speed appropriate for the handoff.
A typical numeric distance (lead/head-start length) ahead of the exchange zone at which the outgoing runner should start accelerating.
A specific starting distance (typical numeric mark ahead of the exchange zone) at which the outgoing runner should begin accelerating.
The typical amount of practice time teams devote to rehearsing baton handoff coordination in advance of a competition — a duration quantity not specified in the passage.

The procedure or criteria by which teams recalibrate the outgoing runner's start mark (its placement/distance) for a given pairing of runners, based on their respective speeds and acceleration characteristics, so the handoff occurs at speed within the exchange zone.
The standard length (distance measurement) of the permitted baton exchange zone in relay racing.
The procedures or adjustments teams make to start marks, timing, and handoff execution when the pairing of outgoing and incoming runners changes.

The set of pairing-specific variables (e.g., incoming runner's approach speed and fatigue, outgoing runner's acceleration profile and reaction time) that determine where the outgoing runner's start mark should be placed.
The specified length (distance measurement) of the baton exchange zone in a standard relay race.
The duration of the time window available for completing a baton handoff while both runners are inside the exchange zone (a quantity of time).
The length of the exchange zone — i.e., the distance available within which the baton pass must be completed before the runners exit it.
The decision procedure or criteria coaches use to set each outgoing runner's starting mark, balancing acceleration gains against the risk of an out-of-zone or failed exchange.
The physical length/dimension of the standard baton exchange zone in relay racing, expressed as a measurement.
The standard length (distance measurement) of the permitted baton exchange zone in relay racing.

The decision procedure or criterion coaches use to set each outgoing runner's start mark within the exchange zone, i.e., how the speed benefit of an earlier start is balanced against the risk of a failed or out-of-zone handoff.

The method or procedure by which relay teams arrive at the optimal start-mark distance for a specific runner pairing (e.g., what inputs such as relative speeds, acceleration, and trial rehearsal data are used and how they are converted into a mark placement).
The specified length (distance measurement) of the baton exchange zone in standard relay racing rules.

The decision criterion or method by which coaches determine the optimal starting point for the outgoing runner's acceleration, i.e., how the trade-off between handoff speed and risk of exchanging outside the zone is resolved into a specific start mark.
The standard length measurement (distance) of the relay baton exchange zone.
The physical length (distance measurement) of the permitted baton exchange zone.
The standard length (distance measurement) of the permitted baton exchange zone in a typical relay race.
The typical length (distance measurement) of the permitted baton exchange zone in a relay race.
The standard length (distance measurement) of the permitted baton exchange zone in a relay race.
The specified physical length (distance measurement) of the legal baton exchange zone in a relay race

The procedure or adjustment rule teams use to reposition the outgoing runner's start mark to accommodate differing speed combinations between paired runners, so the handoff falls within the exchange zone at speed.
The penalty or sanction applied to a team when a baton exchange occurs outside the permitted exchange zone.

The set of runner-pair-specific variables (e.g., relative acceleration profiles, top speeds, reaction and closing rates) that fix where the outgoing runner's start mark should be placed for that pairing.
The method or procedure teams use to set each pairing's start mark (how the correct distance/timing cue is determined or calibrated), not merely the fact that marks vary by pairing.
The standard length, in units of distance, of the baton exchange zone in relay racing.
The method or criteria teams use to determine the starting position/mark governing the incoming runner's approach so that the handoff timing aligns with the outgoing runner.
The physical length (distance measurement) of the permitted baton exchange zone.

The factors that set where an outgoing runner's start mark should be placed — i.e., the pairing-specific variables (relative speeds/acceleration of the two runners, incoming runner's closing velocity, outgoing runner's acceleration profile and reaction timing) that determine the optimal mark position so the handoff occurs at speed within the zone.
The method or procedure by which relay teams work out where the outgoing runner's start mark should be placed for a given pairing of runners.

The method or procedure by which a relay team establishes the correct start-mark distance for a particular outgoing/incoming runner pairing, i.e., the inputs (relative speeds, acceleration, reaction timing) and process (calculation or trial-and-error rehearsal) used to set that mark.

The method or procedure by which relay teams calculate or establish the optimal start mark position for a given pair of runners (i.e., what inputs and process determine where the outgoing runner begins).
The procedure or adjustment rule teams use to modify start-mark placement in response to a pairing-specific rushed or stretched exchange (i.e., how the mark is moved and on what basis).

The method or decision procedure coaches use to set each outgoing runner's start mark, i.e., the criteria and inputs (e.g., relative runner speeds, acceleration, zone limits, practice trials) that determine the optimal start position.
The procedure or criteria teams use to recalibrate the outgoing runner's start mark position when the pairing of runners changes, so the handoff occurs at speed within the exchange zone.
The set of considerations or variables that govern the coaching decision of the outgoing runner's starting point for acceleration, balancing speed gain against exchange-zone risk.
The typical length, in units of distance, of a relay exchange zone.
The rule-based consequence or penalty applied to the team when a baton exchange occurs outside the permitted exchange zone.

The method or procedure by which relay teams establish the correct start-mark distance for a given outgoing runner (i.e., how the mark is calculated or arrived at from the runners' speeds, acceleration, and rehearsal), rather than merely that marks are rehearsed.

The causal explanation for why a start mark that works for one runner pairing yields a rushed or stretched exchange for another — i.e., the pairing-specific factors (differences in acceleration profiles, top speed, reaction/timing between the incoming and outgoing runner) that make a single rehearsed mark fail to produce a comfortable handoff.
The procedure or basis by which teams modify the outgoing runner's start mark placement to suit the specific speed and acceleration characteristics of a given pair of runners.
The decision procedure or criteria coaches use to set each outgoing runner's start-acceleration mark, balancing speed at handoff against risk of exchange failure.

The factors determining the correct start-mark distance for a specific outgoing/incoming runner pairing — i.e., the pair-specific acceleration and speed characteristics and timing relationship that make the handoff occur at speed within the exchange zone.
The spatial positioning (relative distance and alignment) the incoming runner should maintain with respect to the outgoing runner at the moment of the baton exchange.

The explanation of why the optimal start mark depends on the specific pair of runners — i.e., that the mark is set by the relative acceleration profiles and speeds of the incoming and outgoing runners (closing speed and timing to meet within the zone), not by the fixed distance run.
The standard regulated length (distance measurement) of the relay baton exchange zone in official competition
The procedure or adjustment rules teams use to recalibrate start marks when runner pairings change, i.e., how the mark's placement is modified for different pairings.
The typical distance the incoming runner travels prior to the baton exchange — a quantity (length run before handoff), not the mechanics or timing of the exchange.

focal_unknown_anchor: The coaching choice is where each outgoing runner should begin moving so that speed gains do not create too much exchange risk.
